title: Freya and the Cover
premise: Silas Iversen, a disgraced intelligence analyst living off-grid in coastal Norway, is the only person who remembers Flight 4471 ever existed after its records are scrubbed mid-flight. Hunted by the agency that erased it and the passengers' families who never knew they had someone to mourn, Silas discovers the flight carried a witness to a sanctioned atrocity — and that his own erased past is stitched into the cover-up. To survive, he must trade the identity of the true architect of the erasure, a man he once called a friend, to the one person who can burn the network down. The extraction flight leaves at dawn; Silas boards it having traded his secret, his name, and any chance of ever being remembered himself.
about_author: Tamsin Eastwick is a former maritime insurance investigator who spent a decade reconstructing lost paper trails across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes from a farmhouse on the Jutland coast, where she keeps an archive of documents that officially do not exist.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag by the Door
chapters.summary: Silas Iversen's POV. Establishes his exile in a Norwegian fishing town: packed bag, forged papers, nightly ritual of rehearsing his cover story. A call from an old handler offers him one last contract — verify a passenger manifest for Flight 4471. Emotional beat: weary vigilance, the loneliness of a man perpetually ready to run.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. He pulls the manifest and finds his own alias listed among the passengers — a booking he never made. The flight is airborne now, somewhere over the Norwegian Sea. Emotional beat: creeping dread as professional curiosity curdles into personal terror.

chapters.title: Vanishing Point
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, intercut with air traffic controller Ingrid Vass's logs. Mid-flight, every record of 4471 evaporates: radar traces, bookings, crew files. Ingrid remembers the blip; her system insists she doesn't. Emotional beat: gaslit vertigo — reality rewriting itself while two strangers hold the same impossible memory.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Ingrid's POV. She contacts Silas, the only other name attached to the flight's records. They meet in a truck stop; she shows him a passenger's dropped boarding pass that survived the purge. Emotional beat: wary alliance between two people the world has decided are mistaken.

chapters.title: Three Agencies, Three Exits
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, flashback-heavy. We learn why he was bounced: each dismissal followed his refusal to sign off on an 'anomaly resolution.' His old mentor, Casper Lindqvist, signed every one. Emotional beat: bitter self-knowledge — he wasn't fired for incompetence but for honesty.

chapters.title: Hollow Hangar
chapters.summary: Silas and Ingrid reach the airfield where 4471 landed. The hangar is empty, freshly painted, the tarmac resurfaced. But Silas finds tire impressions and a fuel receipt with a tail number. Emotional beat: cold fury — the erasure was thorough, which means it was expensive, which means it was authorized.

chapters.title: What the Tail Number Buys
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The tail number traces to a shell company whose director list includes Casper Lindqvist. Silas realizes his mentor ran the scrub — and that Silas's own alias on the manifest means he was meant to be on that plane. Emotional beat: betrayal sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Passengers of Record
chapters.summary: Ingrid's POV. She identifies one un-erased thread: a grieving sister in Oslo, Marta Holm, whose brother was on 4471 — though official records say he died in a car crash years ago. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into relentless investigation.

chapters.title: The Sister Who Kept Receipts
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. She shows them her brother Elias's hidden drive: he was a financial auditor who found payments routing through the flight's shell company to a black site program. Emotional beat: the price of survival made flesh — Elias hid evidence instead of fleeing, and it killed him.

chapters.title: Contract Renewal
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The 'one last contract' is revealed as bait: Lindqvist wanted Silas close, to confirm what he remembered before deciding whether Silas needed erasing too. A wet team hits the safehouse. Emotional beat: hunted again, but this time knowing exactly who holds the leash.

chapters.title: Runway Lights
chapters.summary: Ingrid's POV. Flight from the safehouse through fog-bound backroads; Ingrid takes a bullet graze shielding the drive. They shelter in a decommissioned lighthouse. Emotional beat: trust cemented in blood — Ingrid chooses Silas's war over her own clean record.

chapters.title: The Drive Decrypted
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The drive contains flight manifests, payment ledgers, and a video: Elias alive post-'death,' testifying about the program. The final file is locked behind a passphrase Silas recognizes — a phrase only he and Lindqvist ever used. Emotional beat: horror that his own history is the key to everything.

chapters.title: Anomaly Resolution
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, deep flashback. The truth of his firings: he once flagged the program's precursor operation, and Lindqvist protected him by getting him quietly dismissed rather than disappeared. His disgrace was a mercy. Emotional beat: devastating reframe — his shame was someone else's shield.

chapters.title: Dawn Is a Deadline
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. An extraction offer arrives through Elias's old channels: a dawn flight out of Bodø for anyone holding the drive. But accepting it means handing the evidence to a faction within the program itself. Emotional beat: the trap inside the rescue.

chapters.title: Lindqvist Calls Collect
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Lindqvist reaches him directly: come in, trade the drive, live under new paper forever — or be erased like the flight. Silas hears the old affection beneath the threat. Emotional beat: the seduction of surrender, almost irresistible to an exhausted man.

chapters.title: The One Secret Worth Killing For
chapters.summary: Ingrid's POV. Silas confesses his real secret: the locked file names not Lindqvist but the program's actual architect — a sitting minister whose protection makes everyone else expendable. Lindqvist was the janitor, not the killer. Emotional beat: the weight of being the only vessel of a dangerous truth.

chapters.title: Bodø, Before First Light
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. They set the exchange: the drive for the extraction seats, with Marta feeding a copy to journalists as insurance. The wet team closes in; Ingrid stays behind as decoy. Emotional beat: sacrifice staged in freezing pre-dawn dark.

chapters.title: Boarding Pass, One Way
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. At the airfield, Silas trades the drive — but hands over the decrypted file naming the minister, keeping only the ledger proving Lindqvist's mercy. The extraction plane idles; the minister's people realize too late what they've been given. Emotional beat: the trade made with steady hands and a breaking heart.

chapters.title: Climax: Cleared for Takeoff
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. As the plane rolls, the minister's strike team storms the runway; Lindqvist arrives and turns his own security against them, buying the takeoff with his life. Radio traffic confirms the file reached prosecutors abroad. Emotional beat: catharsis paid for in full — survival achieved, innocence gone.

chapters.title: Aftermath: Records Restored
chapters.summary: Ingrid's POV. Weeks later, Flight 4471 reappears in the public record; the minister resigns under investigation; Elias Holm is posthumously acknowledged. Ingrid receives a package: the boarding pass, returned, with no note. Emotional beat: quiet vindication that feels insufficient against the losses.

chapters.title: The Man Without a File
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, new identity in Lisbon. He unpacks the go-bag for the first time in years — then packs it again, lighter. A news alert: the program's remnants are stirring. Emotional beat: peace as provisional, survival as ongoing discipline.

chapters.title: Freya and the Cover
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, coda. He learns 'Freya' was the flight's callsign — and the name Elias gave his evidence archive. Silas mails Marta the ledger clearing Lindqvist, keeps only the boarding pass, and walks into the city unnamed. Emotional beat: acceptance — some survivals mean choosing to be no one, so others can finally be remembered.
